title: Which way a fixed-integer price holds
heading: The Price Holds Only With the Plan Fixed and Inside Its Range
cases: with the continuous variable strictly inside its bounds, a small raise of the limit changes the fixed plan's value by price x step
a small cut loses price x step too, and each check moves the limit from its original value, not from where the other check left it
a step past what the continuous variable can absorb, or a cut it cannot absorb, does not hold, even when the fixed plan stays feasible
the price is read with the integers fixed at the plan, not merely relaxed
